PRINCE Trial Biomarker Analysis (DA-9-7): C2D1 CyTOF-Olink Correlation

Summary:
The relationship between circulating immune-cell frequencies and serum
protein levels at C2D1 is treatment-arm-dependent. A pooled (all-arms)
analysis found no significant correlations (0/16 tests at FDR < 0.05).
However, stratified analysis reveals a strong, arm-specific signal.

Key finding:
In Arm C2 (chemo + nivolumab + CD40 agonist combination), HLA-DR+
Non-Naive CD4 T cell frequency negatively correlates with serum IFN-γ
(Spearman r = -0.627, p = 0.003, FDR q = 0.049, n = 20). This
relationship is not present in Arm A1 (chemo + nivolumab, r = +0.112)
or Arm B2 (chemo + CD40 agonist alone, r = +0.222). A formal
interaction test confirms that treatment arm significantly modifies
the cell-population-vs-protein relationship (F-p = 4.5e-4, q = 0.007,
eta-squared-p = 0.23, a large effect).

The finding is robust to jackknife sensitivity analysis (r range
-0.57 to -0.69 across all leave-one-out iterations) and is not driven
by baseline differences in IFN-γ levels or T cell frequencies between
arms (Kruskal-Wallis p > 0.2 for both variables across arms).

A similar but weaker pattern is seen for HLA-DR+ Non-Naive CD8 T cells
vs IFN-γ in Arm C2 (r = -0.480, p = 0.032, q = 0.172, nominal trend).

The negative correlation in the combination arm may reflect activated
CD4 T cell trafficking from blood to tissues during dual checkpoint +
costimulatory therapy, with local IFN-γ production in tissues and
reduced circulating activated T cell frequencies.

Limitations: Small arm-specific sample sizes (n = 20-25), only 4 cell
populations and 4 proteins available at C2D1, 20% missing CyTOF data
in Arm C2, and a single on-treatment timepoint precludes causal
inference.
